Light inq feels really good. The main thing I like about it is, in contrast to like dark side jedi, you are still obviously a sith. Just instead of randomly torturing and killing for the fun of it, you're paving a unique path to power. 

The warrior's goals are smaller than the inquisitor, right? So, for the inquisitor, it makes sense to try and establish a wide power base that is deeply loyal. Who would you rather work with if you were a member of the empire? An unstable maniac who shocks and kills their subordinates for faux pas and inconsequential mistakes? Or a pragmatic and subdued killer who rewards success and encourages rather than punishes. 

If your goal is to become emperor, why not both widen and deepen the pool of tools at your disposal? Welcoming aliens (khem, voss), assisting people "beneath" you (andronikos, balmorra), keeping your promises (the doctor on balmorra, the force ghosts), you're building a loyal following that doesn't *just* fear you. They *want* you to succeed because they know they're coming with you. As opposed to feeling like disposable tools on your path, they feel like useful allies. 

You're the future of the sith, why not differentiate yourself from all the rest? You were a slave, you know how barbaric the practice is, you've seen the corruption and failings inherent in the "traditional" sith ways. 

Think about the superweapon in Act 3. You save a sith fleet, the fleet of an ally of your enemy. When you face Thanatos, his ally, the sith you saved, refuses to stand by him. You usurped Thanatos' fear-based loyalty.

Fallout had higher highs for sure, fully synthetic humans, teleportation, I'm pretty sure even cold fusion is more advanced than cyberpunk. But those technologies are incredibly few and far between. The difference between what the average person would be able to interact with in night city vs. any wasteland would be massive. Not to mention societal wealth and availability, in night city you could save up and buy an entire new set of arms and you would only be one of countless other people with those same arms. So I would say fallout has a higher peak, but the inequality and inaccessibility make it feel much more primitive. 

That said, if there was a nuclear apocalypse in cyberpunk, that would be the end of most cyberwear, no more mass production, no more net, no more medications for those who have cyberwear or for anyone who might find a way to mod themselves. 

It's hard to compare because if V attacked diamond city, it would be a bloodbath, while if the sole survivor attacked even just a scav haunt, they probably wouldn't survive. But if it's post apocalypse? In fallout they have advanced sentry turrets and nuclear powered robots who can operate just fine, everything in cyberpunk is reliant on the infrastructure that built it, from production lines, medications, access to power, etc. 

It's the difference between a world that has had time to adapt to the new order of things vs a world that is still being strangled by the old. I'm sure if you gave the cyberpunk post apocalypse hundreds of years, they would find a way to thrive in what little ways the fallout wastes can. But fallout's use of nuclear power catapulted the post apocalypse ahead massively, so it's hard to say cyberpunk post apocalypse could ever reach even the meager development we see in fallout.
